subject: Request: SLA carve-out for customer-managed VPC (Immutecor)
messages:
From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@immutecor.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: david.liu@immutecor.ai, procurement@immutecor.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carve-out for SLA on customer-managed VPC

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about the latency numbers on hosted runs. We are moving forward with a Private deployment in our GCP VPC (customer-managed control plane) and have a couple of procurement blockers related to the SLA.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood provide a targeted carve-out that removes the uptime and 99th-percentile latency commitments for the portions of the stack that run on our customer-managed network (e.g., VPC peering, Cloud NAT, on-prem ExpressRoute)?
2) We need a short shared-responsibility table and an audit artifact that maps Redwood's managed services vs Immutecor's network and storage components.

Procurement needs this week — can you circulate a proposed carve-out text and a simple network diagram we can include in the SOW? I’ve attached our current network topology (network-diagram-immutecor.pdf).

Thanks,
Aisha Patel
Head of Cloud Ops
Immutecor Therapeutics
[attachment: network-diagram-immutecor.pdf (pdf)]

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@immutecor.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for SLA on customer-managed VPC

Hi Aisha —

Appreciate the clarity and the diagram. We can accommodate a carve-out but need to align legal + infra first. I’ve looped in Vivek (infra) and Marissa (acct exec) so we can propose language that is technical correct and procurement-friendly.

I’ll follow up with a draft carve-out and a short shared responsibility table by end of day tomorrow.

Best,
Neha
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[signature]

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for SLA on customer-managed VPC

Quick tech notes — copying what we need to be explicit about so legal can draft precise carve-out language: 

- Scope: Any network or compute components that are explicitly provisioned, managed, or configured by Immutecor (GCP VPC, on-prem gateways, NAT rules, customer-managed LB) are out of Redwood uptime and latency SLOs.
- Fallbacks: When a downstream (customer) network failure causes a degraded path we need an automatic fallback to the nearest compatible region/variant. That fallback is not guaranteed in a customer-managed topology unless they enable the cross-region peering option (cost/ops tradeoff).
- Observability: We require either (a) shared access to the Immutecor network health page (monitoring read-only role) or (b) daily exported flow logs (CUR/NetFlow) for SLA dispute windows. No access = no SLA claims.
- KV cache and prefix caching: Because KV cache residency impacts token-latency heavily, any on-prem cache managed by Immutecor is excluded from our per-token latency commitments.

I’ll draft the technical carve-out and attach the proposed doc. Also recommend a 30-day post-go-live review where we jointly measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99.

Vivek
Head of Infra — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed carve-out language (draft attached)

Team —

Draft attached: proposed-sla-carveout-draft.docx. Key negotiation points for procurement: 
- Replace blanket uptime guarantees for customer-managed network components with availability assurance for the Redwood-managed runtime only (we retain SLA on our control plane and model-serving nodes we host).
- Add requirement that Immutecor maintains documented incident response contact and provides network flow logs on request within 48 hours for SLA disputes.
- Add a clause that latency SLOs apply only when the end-to-end path includes Redwood-managed ingress (i.e., not for customer WAN-only paths).

Karthik: can you review the legal phrasing on the fallback/indemnity bullet?

Marissa
Acct Exec — Redwood Inference
[attachment: proposed-sla-carveout-draft.docx]

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@immutecor.ai>, David Liu <david.liu@immutecor.ai>, procurement@immutecor.ai
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed SLA carve-out and shared responsibility table — Immutecor

Hi Aisha / David / Procurement,

Thanks for the patience. Attached is our proposed carve-out and a one-page shared-responsibility table that maps network, storage, and orchestration responsibilities. Highlights:

- Effective carve-out: Redwood uptime and p99 latency SLOs are not applicable to failures or latency increases demonstrably caused by customer-managed networking, DNS, or on-prem infrastructure.
- Evidence: For SLA eligibility Immutecor must provide either read-only monitoring access or exported flow logs for the disputed window.
- Cache residency: Any KV cache hosted / controlled by Immutecor is excluded from per-token latency calculations.
- Post-go-live: 30-day joint performance validation and an optional optimization run by Redwood to tune batching/quantization (scope/cost to be a separate SOW).

Please find the draft and our network diagram reference attached. If this aligns, we can move the language into the SOW and have legal teams finalize.

Attachments: proposed-sla-carveout-draft.docx, network-diagram-immutecor.pdf

Next steps we propose:
1) Procurement reviews + redline (target: 48 hours)
2) Provide monitoring access or export of flow logs for the test week
3) Joint go-live performance validation window (30 days)

Appreciate it —
Neha

From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@immutecor.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@immutecor.ai, david.liu@immutecor.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA carve-out and shared responsibility table — Immutecor

Neha —

This looks good and addresses the majority of our procurement concerns. A few small asks from legal: they want "read-only monitoring access" defined to include specific GCP Monitoring metrics and at least seven days of flow logs retention during the go-live validation window. Procurement attached their redline and network team attached a kv-cache ops archive for review.

We are happy to proceed with the SOW insertion pending two changes that we can handle on our side:
- Add explicit mention of "7-day exported VPC flow logs during go-live"
- Confirm a 30-day joint validation window (we accept details around optional RD optimization SOW)

Attaching: procurement-redline.pdf, kv-cache-ops-log-202703.zip

Thanks,
Aisha
[attachment: procurement-redline.pdf, kv-cache-ops-log-202703.zip]
